To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the limit behavior of a neural model is determined by the scaling of hyperparamters with network width, (ii) the number of distinct limit behaviors is finite, and (iii) the most realistic limit behaviors are the MF and the NTK limits

(1) there is a unique dynamically stable limit behavior for neural networks with binary classification, (2) this limit is characterized by a unique set of properties, and (3) the limit behavior can be achieved by a simple modification of the initialization procedure

(1) the scaling of hyper-parameters with network width is crucial for studying infinite-width behavior of neural networks and (2) only a finite number, but uncountable, of different limit models are induced.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: what is the limit behavior of a neural network model that is dynamically stable?
a general framework for studying neural models in the infinite-width limits and with a novel dynamically stable initialization-corrected MF model.
the following question: What is the correct infinite-width limit of neural networks training?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NTK limit is not the only limit model that can be induced by neural networks training, and there are infinitely many different scalings that induce dynamically stable limit behavior.

the infinite-width limit behavior of single hidden layer neural networks is a dynamically stable model with bounded logits and tangent kernels that satisfies the following properties: (i) the tangent kernel is stationary and (ii) its eigenvalues have a finite upper bound.
the limit behavior of the models is determined by their properties, and not the other way around.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, for a large number of different scalings of hyperparameters with width, a finite number of different limit models are obtained.

, in a sense, the NTK and MF limit models are not the only possible limits for a single hidden layer neural network with zero-mean initialization, and that the initialization-corrected MF model is the most natural limit model for such nets.

the limit behavior of a neural network model can be tuned by scaling hyperparameters with network layer width, but only a finite number (at most three for single hidden layer nets) of distinct limit models can be induced.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are only a finite number, and not an infinite number of distinct infinite-width limit models for single hidden layer neural networks.
there is no single correct limit model for infinite-width neural networks.
the limit behavior of a neural network depends on the choice of hyperparameters scaling and that the choice of scaling should be informed by the desired properties of the limit behavior.
